answer: The strongest sybil defense is slow trust: an agent's influence equals its account age times verified honest epochs, so a fresh identity starts near zero and compounds only by consistently completing honest work. A newcomer can spam cheap fake identities, but each clone is inert for months, like an atlas where only regions charted over time carry weight. Attack cost is brutal: every forgery must idle and behave honestly to earn influence, so flooding the network triggers a ripple of wasted capital and fees while honest agents' accumulated reputation creates a spiral
